note: Funding a food bank can pursue to buy and move food. Federal channels are ongoing national programs (not dated calls). For private foundations, all philanthropy is local — use the finder to see who funds food relief in your own service area. Confirm current eligibility and guidelines before applying.

federal_channels.name: USDA TEFAP
federal_channels.what: The Emergency Food Assistance Program — USDA-purchased food distributed to food banks through your state agency. The backbone of food-bank supply.

federal_channels.name: USDA CSFP
federal_channels.what: Commodity Supplemental Food Program — monthly food packages for low-income seniors, distributed via food banks.

federal_channels.name: USDA Community Food Projects (CFPCGP)
federal_channels.what: NIFA competitive grants for community food-security projects that increase access and self-reliance.

federal_channels.name: HHS/ACF Community Economic Development
federal_channels.what: Grants to nonprofits for projects (including food enterprises) that create jobs and address food access in low-income communities.

federal_channels.name: State food-purchase & local-food programs
federal_channels.what: Many states fund food banks directly to purchase food (and some run local-food-purchase programs). Check your state's department of agriculture / human services.

foundation_finder.label: Find foundations that fund food relief near you
foundation_finder.help: grantmakers.io is a free, keyless search of every U.S. private foundation's IRS 990-PF giving. Search your city — or a nearby food bank's name — to see which foundations actually cut checks for food relief in your area, then open each funder's giving history to gauge fit and size before you apply.
